newsitem.title: USA: Lebenthal & Co taps Tankersley as sales director.
newsitem.headline: Lebenthal & Co taps Tankersley as sales director.

text.p: Lebenthal & Co Inc has named Gerald Tankersley, formerly with Prudential Securities Inc, director of sales, a position previously handled by the firm's president, Alexandra Lebenthal.
"We are strengthening the niche that we have in the municipal market," Lebenthal said.

Part of Tankersley's mission will be to help increase the firm's institutional sales market presence by targeting small- to medium-sized institutions. Some institutions have seen coverage fall off as bigger firms cut sales staff.
Lebenthal currently has one main instutitional salesman, Larry Littig, who was hired last year, Lebenthal said.

"I really think that this is a significant move for us, because it does give us the expertise and the manpower to continue moving forward with the company," she said. "We are just coming off of our best year ever."
Lebenthal, who held the sales director's position from 1994 until Friday, was named president as well in 1995.
"I found it very difficult to manage the day-to-day aspects of sales with the long-term strategic planning that the firm very much needs," she said.

Tankersley's appointment also complements another recent hire, she said. Patricia Dolan, a former fund manager at the Prudential, recently joined Jim Gammon at Lebenthal Asset Management Inc as a senior managing director, Lebenthal said.

"I know that there is a real need for coverage of kind of second and third tier accounts, and we think that we are really well-positioned to cover those accounts, particularly maybe trust departments who want to know what the rest of retail is really doing," Lebenthal said.
She emphasized, however, that the firm does not plan to create an institutional sales department that competes with the largest institutional players.
Lebenthal lacks the public finance department to support new issues, she said, adding "and I'm not embarassed to admit that my capital doesn't match Goldman Sachs."

While that may be, Lebenthal plans to grow both in the number of bonds it sells and people it employs, she said. Lebenthal declined to discuss specific hiring plans. The firm currently has a retail sales force of approximately 40.
In addition, because the firm plans to diversify its business, it needs an experienced hand to help develop and introduce new products, she said.
"(Tankersley) has a lot of experience on the Street, which is significant for us, one, because we are a growing organization," Lebenthal said.
Tankersley, a former senior vice president at Prudential where he spent seven years, said he and Lebenthal had spoken about his joining the firm "for some period of time."

"I think you'll see that we are going to broaden the products that we offer our clients," Tankersley said. "I have almost 30 years experience in the business, and have done a lot of different things, so this gives me an opportunity to maybe add some of my experience and skills set to something that already works very, very well."
